newsitem.title: USA: SEC suspends Alliance Ind. trading.
newsitem.headline: SEC suspends Alliance Ind. trading.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced Tuesday that it was temporarily suspending Alliance Industries Inc from trading for 10 days after questions have been raised about the company's Internet home page.
The SEC stated in a suspension order that there was a "lack of adequate and accurate information" about the company's financial projections available through its Internet home page.
The Bakersfield, Calif., company, formerly American Home Alliance Industries, Ltd., is a holding company of five subsidiaries.
Alliance Industries announced last week that it had acquired all common stock, methodology and intellectual property of Carolina Pacific International Inc.
A major business of Alliance Industries is the production of Paulownia trees, a fast growing hardwood. Paulownia is said to grow to sizes harvestable for lumber production in eight to 12 years.
